thesis: Q2 2026 earnings (Aug 4) beat on record revenue (+50% YoY) and data-center growth (+107% YoY), but flat ~56% gross-margin guidance amid AI-chip competition concerns triggered an ~9% post-earnings reversal after a rich pre-print valuation (~48x forward earnings); the slide into early September reflects broad chip-sector/macro rotation (rising yields, seasonal weakness) and a Zacks downgrade, not a new company-specific negative disclosure. Guidance was reaffirmed, not cut, and AMD signed a new AI-compute partnership with Anthropic (up to 2GW, July 22) inside this same window. Conviction is capped at low because the decline reads largely as a technical/valuation reset rather than a disclosed fundamental deterioration -- even though the underlying business signals stayed positive.
invalidation: Q3 2026 results show data-center revenue deceleration or a further gross-margin guide-down, confirming AI-competition margin pressure is structural rather than a one-quarter valuation reset.

thesis: AXTI's 60-day decline caps an extreme round trip -- a pre-earnings low near $37 on 7/29, a blowout Q2 beat (EPS $0.19 vs $0.07 est.) and a Lumentum InP supply deal drove a spike to $97.79 by 8/17, followed by a broad optics/substrate sector selloff after Anthropic's pre-IPO revenue disclosure fell short of 'whisper' expectations (8/17-18) and peer Applied Optoelectronics' new $600M ATM raised dilution-comp fears across the group (8/24). No AXT-specific negative disclosure explains the pullback -- it reads as profit-taking/normalization after a parabolic, sentiment-driven spike. Company insiders sold heavily into the highs (~$78.8M trailing 12 months, zero insider buys) even as sell-side targets stayed in the $90-97 range, while the stock trades at an extreme GAAP P/E (~3,062x) flagged by GuruFocus as still overvalued.
invalidation: Insider buying resumes, or the stock stabilizes well above the pre-earnings base with continued order/backlog confirmation, arguing the pullback has fully digested the speculative spike.
sources: MarketBeat (B. Riley PT cut to $52, July 28 2026): https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/b-riley-financial-cuts-axt-nasdaqaxti-price-target-to-5200-2026-07-28/

thesis: Dell's fiscal Q2 FY2027 earnings (Sept 1) beat decisively -- revenue $47.0B (+58% YoY) vs ~$43-44B consensus, EPS $7.04 vs ~$4.87 consensus -- on a record $95B AI-server order backlog and $60.9B in AI orders in the quarter; Dell raised full-year revenue guidance by $25B to ~$192B and EPS guidance to ~$25.50, and the stock rallied to a new 52-week high on ~2.8x average volume. Even though gross margin has compressed (17.8% in Q1 FY27 vs 21.1% a year earlier) as the AI-server mix grows and DRAM/HBM component costs are projected to keep rising, the magnitude of the guidance raise -- not just the earnings beat -- indicates the backlog is already converting into accelerated profit, which is what the margin-compression bear case would need to see fail to hold up.
invalidation: Q3/Q4 commentary shows margin erosion beyond what's already guided, or component-cost pass-through to AI-server pricing fails, undercutting the backlog-to-earnings conversion story.

thesis: Intel's Q2 2026 print (July 23) beat on revenue (+25% YoY to $16.1B, 7th straight quarterly beat) with AI revenue +70% YoY and Foundry landing its first named external customer (Fortinet, July 21) on Intel 4, plus 18A-P entering risk production -- yet shares fell ~26% over the window: a 'sell-the-news' reversal (July 24, -7.9%) as investors focused on raised 2026 capex guidance (>$20B) and continued Foundry losses (~$2.1B/quarter), then a confirmed $20B upsized common-stock offering (priced Aug 10, closed Aug 12) added real dilution, compounded by broad chip-sector/PC-demand and memory-cost pressure into September. This reads more as a valuation reset after a huge prior rally (+144% YTD before the pullback) plus fresh share dilution than evidence of a deteriorating turnaround -- the underlying Q2 print itself was a beat, not a miss.
invalidation: Foundry losses widen further without additional named external customers, or the $20B raise proves insufficient and Intel needs to return to capital markets again within the next few quarters.

thesis: Marvell's ~17% decline spans two confirmed events: July's hyperscaler-capex/competitive-loss sentiment (reports Amazon shifted next-gen Trainium design work elsewhere) and an Aug 27 post-earnings reversal despite a record Q2 (+37% YoY revenue beat, EPS beat, FY27 guide raised to $12B and FY28 to $18B) -- the drop followed disclosure that the largest incremental Google TPU-ecosystem custom-silicon payoff won't land until fiscal 2029, plus a rising custom-silicon revenue mix pressuring near-term margins. The bear case rests on payoff timing and margin mix, not lost demand: guidance was raised, not cut, data-center revenue is 79% of total and guided +60% for the year, and the existing 5-year Amazon custom-silicon agreement remains in place. Sell-side consensus stayed net Buy across ~29-44 analysts.
invalidation: The Google/Amazon design-win pipeline shows further slippage or a competitive loss is confirmed (not just reported), or FY28 guidance is walked back at the next print.
sources: Marvell Investor Relations (Q2 FY27 press release): https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1031/marvell-technology-inc-reports-second-quarter-of-fiscal-year-2027-financial-results

thesis: Nvidia's Q2 FY2027 earnings (Aug 26) beat decisively -- revenue $96.2B (+106% YoY), Data Center revenue $89.0B (+116.6% YoY, ~92% of total) on the Blackwell Ultra ramp -- and guided Q3 to $108.0B (~89% YoY) plus 70% FY2028 revenue growth vs ~44% the Street expected, driving an 8.7% single-day rally, the stock's largest since April 2025, even though the prior four quarters had each seen post-earnings declines despite beats. Management stated supply, not demand, is the binding constraint. The strongest counter-case -- that Nvidia's ~$750B+ in AI-infrastructure deals (including financing/backstop arrangements with SK Group and OpenAI) resemble circular vendor-financing that could be inflating reported demand optics -- does not change this read: the Q2 beat and Q3/FY28 guide are Nvidia's own already-reported results, not projections built on those financing structures, so even if hyperscaler capex eventually digests, the disclosed catalyst here is already-realized revenue and guidance, regardless of how the financing-structure debate resolves.
invalidation: Q3 FY2027 results miss the $108B guide, or commentary shows hyperscaler capex pulling back in a way that shows up in Nvidia's own order book rather than remaining speculative.

thesis: SPCX's ~12% 60-day decline masks a sharper round trip -- a ~32% drawdown to ~$108-109 by early August (Starship Flight 13 booster-landing failure July 24, then Q2 earnings Aug 4 showing revenue +92% YoY beating estimates but capex jumping 6x QoQ to $18.4B) followed by a ~30%+ rally into month-end on 13F disclosures showing large institutional buying (a ~$21B Nvidia stake, plus Alphabet/AMD/Harvard positions). A confirmed $60B all-stock Cursor/Anysphere acquisition closed Aug 14, issuing ~389M new shares, and staggered post-IPO lockup unlocks are adding tradable float through December -- real, disclosed dilution/supply-overhang mechanics layered on top of the earnings-driven capex-spending concern, rather than a single clean catalyst.
invalidation: Further Starship test failures delay the Starlink v3/launch cadence materially, or Q3 results show the capex ramp outpacing revenue growth without a clear near-term payoff.

thesis: Vertiv's Q2 2026 report (July 29) showed an organic-growth miss (17.8% vs ~23.6% consensus) despite an EPS beat (+60%) and a raised full-year guide, triggering an ~17% single-day drop that was compounded by a broader AI-capex sentiment selloff across data-center/chip names through August. Management called the shortfall 'temporary...supply chain congestion and multi-phased project execution,' and orders were up ~46% YoY with a backlog still reported in the high single-digit billions -- but Vertiv is also discontinuing quarterly order/backlog disclosure going forward, reducing visibility into the very demand metric the bull case depends on, so the backlog-strength counter-case only partially offsets the execution-timing concern raised by the miss itself.
invalidation: Q3 2026 organic growth again falls short of guidance, confirming the July shortfall was not merely a timing issue, or detail on the discontinued backlog disclosure suggests demand itself (not just reporting) is decelerating.

thesis: Victoria's Secret's Q2 FY2026 report (this morning, Sept 3) beat on EPS ($0.95 vs ~$0.75-0.78 consensus) and delivered a 5th straight quarter of positive comps (+9%), with full-year guidance raised -- yet shares fell sharply intraday on weak Q3 operating-income guidance ($10-20M vs prior-year near-breakeven), implying steep sequential margin compression from decelerating comps and rising tariff/freight costs; one outlet also flagged that the Q2 EPS beat was partly aided by a one-time tariff refund. The raised full-year guide and pre-earnings analyst target increases soften the bearish read somewhat, but don't fully resolve it -- the specific disappointment is on forward margin, the metric bulls were extrapolating from, and that remains an open question rather than one this print answers.
invalidation: Q3 results show operating income tracking meaningfully above the new $10-20M guide, or management clarifies the tariff/freight cost pressure is transitory rather than structural.
